name: Can I remain living in my home during an interior renovation?

mainEntity.name: Can I remain living in my home during an interior renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether you can stay in your home depends on which rooms are being renovated and the level of disruption to essential services. If work is limited to a basement, guest bath, or single bedroom, homeowners generally remain in the house with proper dust containment and work-zone barriers in place. If the project involves your only full bathroom or a complete kitchen tear-out, living through the renovation requires setting up temporary cooking areas or finding short-term accommodations during intensive phases like framing, subfloor work, and drywall sanding.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, for isolated areas like basements or spare rooms. Whole-home remodels or sole-bathroom and kitchen projects often require temporary arrangements during heavy demolition and dust phases.
